questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Firstly, I felt a strong connection to the destination having travelled there on numerous occasions, and it felt familiar and safe. Secondly, I had an extremely good impression of my host university. The courses matched my interests very well and I knew other students who had a great experience with the University of Edinburgh. Although I was very set on this university from the beginning, I felt that all of my needs were met - personally and academically.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Such a great and progressive university with so many opportunities outside of academia. There were many groups and societies to join with all kinds of special interests.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. The study abroad team at my host university were consistent with check up emails and events to make sure everything was done correctly. Very kind reception and understanding to the fact that you are a new visiting student.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The visiting students team held an online meeting to go through the steps of matriculation. What to do and check up, how to do it, so i felt looked after in this process.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I applied through my host institution and even though they do not guarantee housing for single semester students, I was told there was a fair chance to find accommodation. The application process was simple and easy to understand and I received an accommodation offer 2 months before departure. I would definitely recommend applying through the host institution.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Accommodation is generally close to campus, at least in my case. The accommodation team is quite friendly and do regular checkups on your living situation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very satisfied and very few complaints. Of course the housing standards aren't luxurious, but perfectly livable. However, I had to purchase almost everything from kitchenware to bedding, so the flat was quite empty upon arrival, and getting rid of these things on moving day was a little inconvenient.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The visiting students team made sure to go through the steps with me, so i felt it was quite easy and simple. Of course there is a lot of steps, but it is perfectly doable.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration was part of the matriculation process, in which there are four steps as I recall. These steps must be completed in order to be accepted into the host institution. It is register as student, complete international checkin, confirm attendance (which the visiting students team will help you do) and pay tuition fees (not applicable to erasmus exchange)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The visiting students team at my host university made sure to do regular checkups and reminders and they held an online event where attendance was confirmed and explained the other steps. They are easy and quick to contact in case you need help. You are also assigned one 'personal tutor' who will be your contact during the exchange.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fairly succesful. I did my exchange on my 4th semester, which unfortunately meant that I did not have the prerequisites for quite a few courses. And I did a subject specific exchange, which meant there were some limitations in choosing courses. However, I did end up with the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not worry about unintentionally missing steps, the visiting students team are with you every step of the way and are very helpful. However, do note down deadlines, so you have an overview of when to do what. Get to know the specifics of your exchange, as well as the prerequisites for the courses, so you know which courses you are eligible for - that could have saved me some time in choosing my courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level is definitely doable. I did not feel too stressed or felt that I was behind. I chose year 2 courses which matched very well with the level I was at. I know you can choose year 1 courses which are less demanding. But I would say that the level is not very different from what I was used to, and I never felt that at assignment or exam was too difficult to tackle.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More or less same format with lectures and seminars. However, the seminar classes were quite small with only 10-12 students and shorter, typically lasting just one hour - so, speaking up was quite easy.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
English in Time and Space
Songs, Swords, Rebel and Revivals: Modern Celtic Literature in Translation
Literary Studies: English Literature post 1789

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: University of Edinburgh offers many courses with a focus on Scottish language, literature, history and culture, so I would definitely recommend doing something that relates to the country. It's a fun way to learn about the place you are visiting, and you feel even more connected to it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Housing was a little more expensive that I first expected/hoped for. But the cost of living is lower than in DK, so it was manageable.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping was generally cheaper than back home, so you can live on a budget. I only had to buy books for one course, so that was helpful. Materials from other courses were all online. Some societies require a fee for membership, but not all.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Countless possibilities. During introduction week, they do taster sessions for all the clubs/societies and there are truly too many to count. No doubt you will find something that you will find fun/interesting.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend joining a club/society. It's a great way to meet new friends with similar interests as yourself. I joined an equestrian club (which was quite expensive, but very fun), and met some great people there.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Edinburgh is a very walkable city (low cost on transport), so stroll around during the weekends. Many museums are free, so that's another great option. Some societies also do day trips to the countryside/highlands for a low price and that's a great way to get out of the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Scotland is not too different from Denmark. Very safe place and sociable people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies, that is by far the easiest way. And there are so many places around campus to meet up, study, have coffee together.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There is so much pride in the Scottish history that you can feel all over the city. The Scots definitely cherish their culture and that is very easy to see when you walk around Edinburgh. You can almost always hear a bagpipe playing and the pubs and bars are always full of people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't worry too much about the academic level - some things are challenging, but it's perfectly doable. And they want you to feel comfortable and do well on the courses. 
2. Join a society!
3. Take time to explore the city - Edinburgh is magical, and there are so many places to see and the Scottish culture will definitely get under your skin.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Spend some time checking the prerequisites for the courses - that can be a bit challenging. 
Try to find accommodation in the city centre. Edinburgh is a quite small city and very walkable, and you will save money on transport. University of Edinburgh is very inclusive and progressive and they definitely try to meet your needs.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people that will hopefully stay in my life for many years. Trying to live abroad and manage the exchange on my own also strengthened my self confidence. I definitely feel more brave and optimistic about my personal and academic future. While the whole experience might seem scary at first, you will feel more self assured when you complete the exchange.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Of course having the whole semester in front of you is quite frightening, but to be honest I never struggled that much. I think my greatest worry was if I did well enough in my assignments and try to get a sense of what was expected of me - but that turned out just fine. Also putting yourself out there socially can be intimidating, as you are taken out of your usual setting.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I warmly recommend University of Edinburgh. I had an absolutely amazing experience and would never be without it. I have learned so much about myself and what I want to do with my education. Living and studying abroad has been incredibly rewarding for me and has made me feel more self assured personally and academically.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
